title: DHCP Systems: Infrastructure & Leasing
subject: DHCP Core Services
description: Master the logic of dynamic addressing. Resolve issues with broadcast boundaries, lease exhaustion, and failover synchronization using an evidence-first workflow.
reportOverview: This report evaluates your ability to manage IP distribution. Key skills tested: DHCP Relay (IP Helpers), Scope management, Failover MCLT logic, and Authorization.
evidenceInstructions:
Instructions:
1) Read the user's complaint.
2) Use the initial step to gather evidence.
3) Diagnose the logic error.
4) Apply the Fix and review the Resolution Insight to see why your solution worked.

tickets.title: New DHCP Server Inactive
tickets.summary: You've installed DHCP on the new Domain Controller. The service is running, but the console shows a red down arrow and no IPs are being handed out.

triage.q: What is the first thing to check in the console for a new domain-joined DHCP server?

diagnosis.q: Why is the server 'Running' but inactive?
options: The server must be Authorized in AD to prevent 'Rogue' DHCP servers

fix.q: How do you activate the server?

debrief.summary: DHCP servers need 'permission' to work in a Windows domain.
debrief.takeaway: Resolution Insight: Just because a service is 'On' doesn't mean it's 'Active.' In a domain, DHCP servers must be authorized to prevent someone from accidentally plugging in a personal router and breaking the network's IP scheme. Authorization ensures only trusted servers talk to clients.

tickets.title: Cross-Subnet Connectivity Failure
tickets.summary: Users on Floor 2 (different VLAN) are getting 169.254.x.x addresses, while Floor 1 (where the server is) works fine.

triage.q: DHCP Discover packets are broadcasts. What does a router do with them by default?

diagnosis.q: Why is Floor 2 failing to reach the server?
options: The router is blocking the broadcast from crossing to the other subnet

fix.q: What is the industry-standard fix on the router?

debrief.summary: Routers act as barriers for DHCP traffic.
debrief.takeaway: Resolution Insight: You identified that the server was working, but the request couldn't reach it. Since broadcasts can't cross routers, the IP Helper acts as a relay, picking up the request on Floor 2 and delivering it directly to the server on Floor 1.

tickets.title: Address Conflict Warnings
tickets.summary: Users are reporting 'IP Address Conflict' popups. The console shows several 'BAD_ADDRESS' entries.

triage.q: What does a 'BAD_ADDRESS' status actually mean?
options: The server detected the IP was already in use before offering it

diagnosis.q: Why is the server finding conflicts?
options: Printers have static IPs that overlap with the dynamic DHCP pool

fix.q: How do you stop the conflicts?
options: Create an 'Exclusion Range' for the static IPs

debrief.summary: Conflict detection protects the network from IP collisions.
debrief.takeaway: Resolution Insight: The server did its job by 'checking the door' (pinging) before offering the IP. By creating an Exclusion, you told the server to stop trying to use those specific IPs for laptops, giving the printers the space they need.

tickets.title: Guest Wi-Fi Pool Exhaustion
tickets.summary: Visitors cannot connect. The DHCP console shows the scope is 100% utilized, even though the lobby is empty.

triage.q: If a scope is 100% full, what happens to the next person who joins?

options: The 8-day lease is holding onto IPs long after guests have left

debrief.summary: Lease duration controls how fast IPs are recycled.
debrief.takeaway: Resolution Insight: You realized the IPs weren't gone; they were just 'reserved' for people who were no longer in the building. Shortening the lease allows the server to reclaim and recycle those IPs much faster for the next guest.

tickets.title: Failover Mismatch Error
tickets.summary: You updated the DNS settings on the Primary DHCP server, but the Secondary server is still giving out old info.

triage.q: Do configuration changes sync automatically in a failover pair?
options: No, they must be manually replicated

diagnosis.q: Why does the secondary have stale info?
options: The change hasn't been 'replicated' to the partner

fix.q: How do you push the new settings?

debrief.summary: Failover keeps leases in sync, but settings require replication.
debrief.takeaway: Resolution Insight: While the servers share the 'list of who has what IP' automatically, they don't share 'rule changes' instantly. Manually replicating ensures both servers are telling the clients the exact same information.

tickets.title: Missing Default Gateway
tickets.summary: Users have an IP but cannot reach the internet. `ipconfig /all` shows no Default Gateway.

triage.q: Which DHCP option tells the client how to reach the internet?

options: The DHCP server isn't configured to send Option 003
Add Option 003 to the Scope Options

debrief.summary: DHCP provides the 'map' to the exit.
debrief.takeaway: Resolution Insight: An IP address tells a computer 'who it is,' but the Gateway tells it 'how to leave.' By adding Option 003, you provided the exit route, proving DHCP is about more than just the address.

tickets.title: NAS Reservation Failure
tickets.summary: A storage device is supposed to be at .200, but it keeps appearing at .105.

triage.q: What does DHCP use to identify a device for a reservation?

options: MAC address typo in the reservation entry

debrief.takeaway: Resolution Insight: You found the typo! DHCP logic is strict: if the ID doesn't match perfectly, the server treats the device like a random guest. Correcting the MAC restores the 'VIP' status of the device.

tickets.title: Short Leases During Outage
tickets.summary: Primary server is down. Users are getting IPs from the backup, but they expire in 1 hour instead of 8 days.

options: The backup uses the MCLT 'safety' duration until the primary returns
No, it is normal behavior during failover

debrief.summary: MCLT is a safety timer for server transitions.
debrief.takeaway: Resolution Insight: You discovered the 'fail-safe.' The secondary server only gives out short leases so that if the primary server wakes up, they don't have overlapping long-term promises. It’s a standard safety feature.

tickets.title: DNS Record Discrepancy
tickets.summary: New devices get IPs, but you can't ping them by name. DNS isn't updating.
artifact: DHCP Settings: DNS dynamic updates disabled
DNS: Records missing for new leases

triage.q: Where is the integration between DHCP and DNS managed?

options: DHCP isn't configured to update DNS records for the clients
Enable 'Dynamically update DNS records' in DHCP

debrief.summary: DHCP acts as a 'secretary' for DNS.
debrief.takeaway: Resolution Insight: You bridged the gap. When DHCP hands out an IP, it should 'call' DNS and update the record. Turning this on ensures your network 'phonebook' stays accurate without manual typing.

tickets.title: Service Startup Error 1067
tickets.summary: DHCP service crashes on startup. Event logs suggest a database error.

triage.q: Where is the physical DHCP database stored?

debrief.summary: DHCP relies on a local Jet database file.
debrief.takeaway: Resolution Insight: You treated DHCP like a database app. When the file gets corrupted, the service can't read its 'to-do list.' Using the backup folder is the fastest way to get back online without losing data.
